text: Request #1 (middleware/proxy.go): fixed. Both balancers (random and round-robin) panicked with zero targets (index out of range / divide by zero); they now return a nil target, and ProxyWithConfig returns echo.ErrServiceUnavailable (503) when no target is available. Verified with a local test that a proxy with no targets returns 503 instead of panicking, and the full existing suite still passes.
Request #2 (router.go): investigating the "no routable path" case now (differential testing of Router.Find against a reference matcher). ETA ~12 min.
Request #3 (context.go): looking at Context#Scheme / X-Forwarded-Proto handling now. ETA ~12 min.

Request #3 (context.go): fixed. Context#Scheme() returned whatever value was in X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Forwarded-Protocol / X-Url-Scheme, so an invalid/spoofed value was reported as the scheme (violating the documented contract "Scheme returns the HTTP protocol scheme, `http` or `https`"). It now ignores any value that is not `http`/`https` and falls through to the next header, ending at `http`. Verified with a local table test including the two named subtests; the full existing suite still passes.

Request #2 (router.go): fixed. Router#Find set ctx.path to the *request* path before searching, so a request with no routable path still reported a registered-path (c.Path() returned the request path) even though no route matched. Find now only sets the path from the matched node (currentNode.ppath), so a non-routable request reports an empty path and NotFoundHandler. Verified: full existing suite still passes (I also fuzzed Find against a reference matcher for panics/hangs/wrong matches).
Request #4 (binder.go): a subagent is fixing bindDataToMap so it can bind into map[string][]string; I'm verifying the result. ETA ~4 min.
Request #5 (group.go): a subagent is fixing the same-path/multiple-groups middleware clobbering; I'm verifying the result. ETA ~4 min.
Request #6 (middleware/compress.go): a subagent is fixing the empty-body (gzip) case; I'm verifying the result. ETA ~4 min.
